Preventive care and cleanings

Keep small questions from becoming bigger surprises

A preventive visit is an opportunity to understand what is happening in your mouth, ask questions, and build a care rhythm that fits your needs. It is also the right entry point when you are looking for a new dental home.

Preventive care includes the practice's confirmed care path for dental checkups, cleanings, and oral-health education. The clinician decides which examination or diagnostic steps are relevant to the visit.

Confirmed care paths

  • Preventive dental exams
  • Dental cleanings
  • Oral-health education and maintenance planning
  • Referral or restorative evaluation when a concern needs a different next step
Practice context

Preventive care and cleanings are identified in the verified public and local service catalogs. No fixed visit frequency or outcome is promised because those decisions are individualized.

01

Who may be a candidate

New patients, returning patients, and people who want to maintain oral health may request a preventive visit.

02

What an online page cannot decide

A routine visit is not a substitute for calling about urgent pain, swelling, injury, or a rapidly changing concern. Visit frequency and the right services vary by patient.

Start with clarity

Your Winter Park consultation

  1. 01

    Share your goals, current questions, and any comfort or scheduling needs.

  2. 02

    Complete the preventive examination and cleaning plan the clinician considers appropriate.

  3. 03

    Leave with the recommended next step, maintenance questions, and any referral or restorative follow-up that applies.

Before you decide

What to expect

The exact visit depends on whether you are new to the practice, returning for maintenance, or asking about a specific concern. The team explains what is included before proceeding.

Tell the office about sensitivity, dental anxiety, or accessibility needs when you schedule. A comfortable visit starts with the team knowing what support would help.

Possible benefits

  • A regular place to ask oral-health questions
  • A chance to identify concerns before deciding on a treatment path
  • Education and maintenance planning that can support long-term care

Limitations & alternatives

  • Preventive visits do not replace urgent evaluation when symptoms change quickly
  • The appropriate frequency and scope vary by patient
  • A separate restorative, periodontal, or surgical evaluation may be needed

After your visit

Care, recovery & maintenance

Follow the oral-hygiene and follow-up guidance provided by the practice. If the visit identifies a need for periodontal or restorative care, use the linked service page and relevant care guide for the next conversation.

Patient resourceReview pre- and post-operative careUse the guide as a supplement to the instructions provided by the practice.

Planning the investment

Insurance & financing questions

Questions patients ask

Start with the questions that matter to you

Is preventive care a good first visit for a new patient?

Yes, a new-patient visit can be a starting point for discussing your goals, completing the appropriate examination and cleaning plan, and understanding next steps.

How often should I schedule a cleaning?

The right interval depends on your oral health and the practice's recommendation. This page does not prescribe a universal schedule.

What if I have pain or swelling?

Call the office directly and explain that the concern may be urgent. A routine appointment request is not the right substitute for prompt guidance.

Can the team discuss sensitive teeth or dental anxiety?

Yes. Mention those concerns when scheduling so the team can include comfort questions in the visit plan.
